findings.summary: The grey arm's direct label is drawn at #929292 (FIVE, line 25) at 14 pt normal weight, measured 3.11:1 against white, below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA threshold for body text; because the figure carries no legend, this label is the only thing telling a reader which trace is the five-worker arm, so a low-vision reader can lose the series identity even though the trace itself meets the 3:1 mark threshold.

rubric_items.contrast: Blue (#2b6cb0, 5.4:1) and near-black annotation text clear body-text contrast on white; the grey arm's own direct label and trace are drawn at #929292, measured 3.1:1 against white, which clears the 3:1 non-text mark threshold but falls short of 4.5:1 for 14 pt normal-weight text, and that label is the only identification of the grey series.
rubric_items.data_ink: The data carry the visual weight: two 2.6/3.0 pt traces with 5 pt markers and one annotation are the only marks; the plot area is otherwise empty and no element competes with the traces.
rubric_items.decoration: No gradient, background fill, gridlines, band or styled theme; top and right spines are removed and only the two scale-carrying spines remain.
rubric_items.label_collision: No label is clipped or overlaps another label or the data: the grey '5 workers / 651 MB' label sits below the trace end, the blue '40 / 655 MB' label above it, and the difference annotation in the clear band above both, all inside the canvas at x up to 8.5 while data end at 7.
rubric_items.legibility: Readable at a glance: a single 14x7.2 in panel, two labelled traces with markers at seven x ticks, y ticks 645-680 MB every 5 MB, and 14 pt text throughout; the arm identity, both medians and the headline delta are all readable without enlarging.
rubric_items.table_form: The image does not depict information that is naturally a table: two time-ordered series over seven samples are a trend comparison, and their medians and difference are stated directly on the figure.

summary: The single attached PNG (the two-arm resident-set figure) was opened and judged on the rendered image only. All six figure rubric items are answered; one non-blocking contrast finding is recorded for the grey arm's direct label. No blocking finding: nothing is clipped, overlapping or unreadable, and both traces and the headline delta are visible.
